sections.h2: What is Bernalillo County and who runs its property tax?
sections.html:
Bernalillo County is New Mexico's most populous county, with 1,160 square miles and more than 676,000 residents, and two elected officials run its property tax: the Assessor values property and the Treasurer bills and collects. The county government also has five commissioners, a clerk, a probate judge and a sheriff.

A county news release says the government serves residents of Albuquerque, Los Ranchos and Tijeras, and that about 106,000 people live in unincorporated areas. Albuquerque is the county seat. Both offices share Alvarado Square at 415 Silver Ave SW. The Assessor can be reached at (505) 222-3700 and the Treasurer at (505) 468-7031.

The Assessor describes its job as valuing real property, business personal property, livestock and manufactured homes, notifying owners and preparing the tax roll for the Treasurer.

sections.h2: How does the Bernalillo County property tax year work?
sections.html:
Value is fixed on January 1, notices go out by April 1, rates are set in September, the roll goes to the Treasurer by October 1, and bills are mailed by early November. Each step comes from the Assessor's FAQ and the Treasurer's pages.

StepTimingWho
Property valued as of its conditionJanuary 1Assessor
Exemption and Head of Family applicationsLast day of February, or 30 days after the Notice of ValueAssessor
Notices of Value mailedBy April 1Assessor
Assessor certifies valuation to the stateJune 15Assessor
Delinquent notices mailedAbout June 10Treasurer
Rates set by stateSeptemberDept. of Finance and Administration
Tax roll deliveredOctober 1Assessor to Treasurer
Bills mailed, first half dueNovember 1 and November 10Treasurer
Second half dueApril 10Treasurer

The 2026 roll was delivered on October 1, and the Treasurer said bills would be mailed by November 2 because November 1 was a Sunday. Owners who are not on the 10-month payment agreement can pay in full or in two installments.

sections.h2: How are Bernalillo County taxes calculated?
sections.html:
Taxable value is one-third of the assessed value, and the exemption comes off that figure before the mill rate is applied. The Assessor's FAQ defines net taxable value as taxable value minus exemptions such as Head of Family and the veterans' exemption.

The state sets the rates. In an October 2025 post, the Treasurer said the Department of Finance and Administration affirmed 2025 mill rates, that many rates fell compared with 2024, and that rising valuation, a new taxing district and additional tax initiatives would still push bills up across the county. Rates differ by taxing district, so the Assessor's property search and the Treasurer's rate charts for 2016 to 2025 are the right places to find a figure for one address.

New Mexico law caps annual growth in taxable value of residential property at 3%, a rule the Doña Ana County Assessor describes and the Bernalillo County Assessor applies to manufactured homes as well. The cap limits assessment growth, not the mill rate.

sections.h2: What tax savings programs does Bernalillo County offer?
sections.html:
The Assessor lists Head of Family, veteran and disabled veteran exemptions and a value freeze. A separate protest form is not needed for any of them.

  • Head of Family takes $2,000 off taxable value for one property per household in the state.
  • The veteran exemption takes up to $10,000 off taxable value with a certificate from the New Mexico Veterans' Service Commission. Once granted, it stays on the record.
  • Disabled veterans can exempt a percentage of the primary residence based on their VA disability rating.
  • The value freeze is for owners 65 or older with modified gross income of $42,900 or less, or disabled owners at $41,900 or less. It stops the assessed value from rising 3% and does not freeze the tax rate.

The deadline for the current year is 30 days after the Notice of Value is mailed. The Assessor's tax savings page has the forms. The FAQ also notes that a value freeze does not force you to sell at the frozen value.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Bernalillo County valuation?
sections.html:
File a protest with the Assessor within 30 days of the Notice of Value mailing, online through the appeal portal or at 415 Silver Ave SW. An informal meeting with a field appraiser follows, and a hearing before the Protest Valuation Review Board comes next if the value is not resolved.

For the 2026 tax year, business personal property, manufactured home and livestock protests ran from May 1 to a June 1 deadline. An owner who received an amended Notice of Value gets 30 days from the amended mailing date.

Someone who misses the window can still pay the bill and file a claim for refund in the Second Judicial District Court at 400 Lomas Blvd NW. The Treasurer says the claim must be filed by the 60th day after the first installment due date and that the bill must be paid first. The court filing fee listed by the Assessor is $132. The Assessor's protest page also gives a January 10 date, so confirm the cutoff with the court self-help center at 505-841-6702 before relying on either.

If a protest is still pending in December, the Treasurer recommends paying the first half on the original bill. A new bill and a refund follow if the protest succeeds, and paying avoids late fees if it does not.

sections.h2: What happens when Bernalillo County property tax is paid late?
sections.html:
Late fees are interest of 1% per month plus a penalty of 1% per month, with the penalty capped at 5% and a minimum of $5. They start December 10 for the first half and May 10 for the second.

The Treasurer accepts payment in person on the first floor of 415 Silver Ave SW, online through the county's payment vendor, or by mail to PO Box 27800, Albuquerque, NM 87125-7800. The office warns against using a bank's bill-pay service, citing mailing delays, misrouting and lack of confirmation. It also says owners are liable even if a bill never arrives, and that roughly 10,600 bills were returned in the 2025 cycle, mostly for outdated addresses.

As of June 2026 the office reported about $917.5 million collected and a rate of nearly 95%. Delinquent notices began mailing June 10.

sections.h2: What should a seller in Bernalillo County know about tax at closing?
sections.html:
The owner of record on January 1 is liable for that year's tax, and a manufactured home needs a tax release before it can be sold, moved or traded. Title companies pull the balance and pay it from the sale proceeds.

The Assessor's FAQ says a manufactured home owner must obtain a tax release from the Treasurer showing current and prior years are paid, and begins that process at the Assessor with proof of ownership. Land and a manufactured home on it get separate notices and bills unless the home has been converted to real property. Public improvement district charges transfer to the buyer, and a seller can prepay the balance.

After closing, file the residential transfer affidavit with the Assessor within 30 days, as covered in our Bernalillo County Clerk guide. Sellers carrying back taxes, an inherited house or a tenant-occupied property often sell as-is for cash to avoid repairs and showings, and the tax balance comes out of the proceeds either way.

faqs.q: When are Bernalillo County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due November 10 and the second half April 10. Late fees begin December 10 and May 10, according to the Bernalillo County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Who sets property values in Bernalillo County?
faqs.a: The elected County Assessor sets values and mails Notices of Value by April 1. The elected Treasurer bills and collects the tax, and the state sets mill rates each September.

faqs.q: How do I protest my Bernalillo County valuation?
faqs.a: File a protest form with the Assessor within 30 days of the Notice of Value mailing, online or at 415 Silver Ave SW. An informal meeting and, if needed, a Protest Valuation Review Board hearing follow.

faqs.q: What exemptions can Bernalillo County homeowners claim?
faqs.a: Head of Family reduces taxable value by $2,000, veterans can claim up to $10,000, disabled veterans can exempt a percentage of their primary residence, and eligible seniors or disabled owners can apply for a value freeze.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bernalillo County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company normally pays the balance, including penalty and interest, from the sale proceeds at closing. Confirm the figure with the Treasurer at (505) 468-7031.

faqs.q: Does Bernalillo County send a bill if a mortgage company pays my taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Every owner receives a bill even when a lender pays. The bill lists the mortgage company that requested the amount, and the owner stays responsible for making sure it is paid.
